# driver

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/driver"
```

Package driver owns module compilation.

A module is the unit of compilation because imports, build constraints, and test packages decide which files form a program. The driver keeps those choices consistent across frontend checking and lowering. It uses Go's build rules so TGo files belong to the same packages as their Go equivalents.

Source files are authoritative. Existing generated files can be stale and must not affect source checking. Compiler work uses a separate directory so compilation does not edit the caller's files.

Compilation passes data through these steps: read module files, prepare a separate work directory, select source with Go's build rules, check source packages, lower expressions, check emitted Go, and collect output. Each step keeps the data required by the next step. Source files stay separate from the files used for checking.

The driver returns the emitted module as file contents. Writing those files belongs to the caller. Expression evaluation rules belong to the lowerer.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string) map[string][]byte
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files and returns file contents by module\-relative path. It keeps other module files in the result and panics on invalid source or compiler failures.
